why: A behavioural mode is *how* the daemon approaches a problem; a Micronaut is the *capability* that performs an operation. Letting a mode own capabilities would make behaviour an execution grant, and duplicating a Micronaut per mode would mean four copies of the same question engine. So a mode only references capabilities, one Micronaut serves many modes, and the registry stays the single source of what is callable.

separation.mode: how the daemon approaches the problem — patterns, bias vectors, question style, response format
separation.micronaut: the capability that performs an operation — registered, versioned, and callable
separation.law: a mode binds preferences; the registry owns the capability; XCFE authorizes the invocation
separation.not_a_node_class: a mode is not an executable node class: the closed 14-class XCFE ISA and the six phases are unchanged, so a new mode never requires a new class

ref_forms.name: a registered Micronaut name, e.g. `eliza`
ref_forms.capability: `cap:<token>`, resolved to every Micronaut declaring that capability, e.g. `cap:question`

binding.weights: routing preferences, not execution permissions: they order candidates and never admit one
binding.multiplicity: a mode may bind several Micronauts and activates them together
binding.sharing: one Micronaut may serve many modes: the same question capability participates in teacher, socratic, investigator and scientist
binding.phase_preferences: a mode may prefer a Micronaut per phase, but the phase keeps its authority and a preference is not a dispatch

resolution.registry: drivers/micronauts/registry.json is the authority for what exists
resolution.distinct_facts: registered and runnable are separate: a Micronaut in the registry with no driver manifest is registered but not runnable (as `cfpc` and `xcfe` are today), and a binding reports both facts rather than collapsing them
refusals: an unknown name is refused, never silently dropped
an unregistered capability token is refused
a binding weight outside [0, 1] is refused
the same reference bound twice is refused
a phase preference naming an unbound or unknown Micronaut is refused

composition.law: Micronauts may call other Micronauts, so capability composes hierarchically without making a mode executable
composition.example: scientist: hypothesis -> {question, math, experiment}, and critic -> cheese
composition.cycle: a call cycle is refused with the path that formed it, because recursive capability would never terminate
composition.depth: composition is bounded by a declared maximum depth; exceeding it is refused
composition.order: a resolution order is a valid topological order of the reachable subgraph

dynamic_recruitment.law: the active mode may shift during the fold, so the preferred capability set can change between phases
dynamic_recruitment.audit: each stage records the mode and the preference set that was active, so a fold shows which capabilities it had available at each phase
dynamic_recruitment.bound: recruitment changes preferences only; it never admits an invocation

invariants.MB1: a mode binds references only — names or capability tokens — and never defines, duplicates or owns a capability
invariants.MB2: binding weights are routing preferences: they order candidates and grant nothing, and no API in this layer can admit an execution
invariants.MB3: a mode may bind and activate several Micronauts simultaneously, and one Micronaut may serve any number of modes
invariants.MB4: resolution is against the shipped registry; an unknown name, an unregistered capability token, an out-of-range weight or a duplicate reference is refused with its own reason
invariants.MB5: registered and runnable stay distinct facts: a Micronaut with no driver manifest is reported registered-but-not-runnable, and is excluded from the runnable set rather than silently treated as available
invariants.MB6: a phase preference is a preference: it hoists a candidate for that phase, it does not dispatch, and naming an unbound or unknown Micronaut is refused
invariants.MB7: Micronaut composition resolves in a topological order of the reachable subgraph
invariants.MB8: a composition cycle is refused and the path that formed it is reported
invariants.MB9: composition depth is bounded; exceeding the declared maximum is refused
invariants.MB10: the six phases and the closed 14-class XCFE node ISA are unchanged: adding a behavioural mode adds no node class and no phase
